verdict.rationale: Gram documents OAuth-based authentication for MCP servers (any OAuth 2.0 provider like Auth0/Okta/Keycloak) which could let individual end users authenticate and scope their own tokens, and RBAC/OAuth2.1 tied to enterprise IDPs for team/role permissions. However, the evidence is framed around enterprise-internal governance (employees/teams synced to a corporate IDP) rather than a platform-engineer managing many discrete end-user 'connected accounts' for their own product's users, and there's no explicit mention of per-end-user credential vaults or multi-tenant token isolation. Missing for 10: explicit multi-tenant/end-user connected-account management, per-end-user token vaulting/isolation documentation, and independent confirmation that each product end-user gets a distinct scoped credential rather than team/role-level access.
